prompt: Before training a cat-or-dog model, the team pays people to tag 10,000 photos with the right answer.
tells: tag 10,000 photos with the right answer
why: People attach the right answer, cat or dog, to each photo so the model can learn from them. Examples with answers attached are labeled data.
trap: The task will be classification, but this step is labeling.

prompt: The model can't learn yet, because none of the past loans record whether they were repaid.
tells: none of the past loans record whether
why: To learn to predict repayment, each example needs the outcome. Without the repaid-or-not answer, the loans have no labels.
trap: Nothing is leaking; the answers are missing.

prompt: A startup pays reviewers to mark each transcript as correct or incorrect for training.
tells: pays reviewers to mark each transcript
why: Reviewers attach the right answer, correct or incorrect, to each transcript. Creating those answers is labeling data.
trap: This happens before training, not at inference.

prompt: Supervised learning needs examples paired with the correct answers.
why: Supervised learning learns by comparing its guesses to correct answers. Examples paired with answers are labeled data.

prompt: The house dataset includes the sale price for every house, so the model can learn from it.
tells: includes the sale price for every house
why: The sale price is what the model is learning to predict, and it's known for every house. That known answer is the label.
trap: It's the target, so it isn't leakage.

prompt: Doctors annotate scans with where the tumor is so a model can learn to find it.
why: Doctors mark where the tumor is on each scan, giving the model the right answers to learn from. Expert annotations are labels.
